headline: Revenue and margins climb as full-year guidance is raised
summary_short: Coca-Cola's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 7% to $13.4 billion and diluted EPS grew 16% to $1.03, as management raised full-year organic revenue and EPS guidance.
summary_long: Revenue grew 7% to $13.38B (organic +6%), driven by 4-point concentrate-sales growth and 2-point price/mix, with volume up 5% led by India, China, the U.S. and Brazil. Operating margin expanded to 34.9% from 34.1% on lower operating expenses and currency tailwinds, partly offset by higher input and marketing costs. Diluted EPS rose 16% to $1.03 (comparable EPS +11% to $0.97), including a 4-point currency tailwind. Cash from operations was $7.5B YTD versus a $1.4B outflow a year earlier; cash and equivalents rose to $12.9B. Management raised FY2026 guidance: organic revenue to ~5% growth, comparable EPS to 9-10% growth, and free cash flow to ~$12.4B.

drivers.explanation: Management said the company gained value share in total NARTD beverages and leveraged its brands, system and FIFA World Cup activation to deliver revenue, profit and earnings growth while investing for the long term.
Growth driven by a 4-point rise in concentrate sales and 2-point price/mix gains; volume grew 5%, led by India, China, the U.S. and Brazil.
Comparable currency-neutral operating income grew 6%, driven by organic revenue growth and lower operating expenses, partially offset by higher input costs and increased marketing investment.

Growth included one-time items -- a $66M reduction of a previously recorded Africa-bottling impairment and other net gains -- per the comparability reconciliation; comparable (non-GAAP) net income grew 11% versus 16% reported.
EPS grew 16% to $1.03, including a 4-point currency tailwind; comparable EPS (non-GAAP) grew 11% to $0.97 with a 2-point currency tailwind.
